description: An overview of Zakah covering its meaning, who must pay it, the eight categories of recipients, nisab, Zakat al-Fitr, and its spiritual and social benefits.

mcq.questionText: Zakah is which pillar of Islam?
mcq.explanation: Zakah is the third pillar of Islam, coming after the Shahadah and Salah.

mcq.questionText: What is the literal meaning of the word 'Zakah'?
mcq.explanation: Zakah literally means purification and growth; it purifies wealth and the heart and increases blessings.

mcq.questionText: How many categories of people are entitled to receive Zakah according to the Qur'an?
mcq.explanation: The Qur'an mentions eight categories of people who are eligible to receive Zakah.

mcq.questionText: What is the minimum amount of wealth a person must own before Zakah becomes due?
mcq.explanation: Nisab is the minimum threshold of wealth that a person must possess for a full year before Zakah becomes obligatory.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the difference between Zakah and Sadaqah?

options.text: Both are obligatory on every Muslim
Zakah is obligatory while Sadaqah is voluntary
Sadaqah is obligatory while Zakah is voluntary
Both are voluntary acts of charity

mcq.explanation: Zakah is a compulsory duty with fixed conditions, whereas Sadaqah is voluntary charity given any time in any amount.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is NOT one of the conditions for Zakah to be obligatory on a person?

options.text: Holding the wealth for one lunar year
Being above the age of forty

mcq.explanation: There is no requirement to be over forty; the conditions relate to faith, ownership of nisab, and possession for a lunar year.

mcq.questionText: The completion of one full lunar year on wealth before Zakah is paid is known as:
mcq.explanation: Hawl refers to the passing of one complete lunar year, a condition for Zakah on most types of wealth.

mcq.questionText: Which category of recipients refers to people whose hearts are to be reconciled or attracted towards Islam?

options.text: Al-Mu'allafah Qulubuhum (those whose hearts are to be reconciled)

mcq.explanation: Al-Mu'allafah Qulubuhum are those whose hearts are to be inclined or reconciled towards Islam, one of the eight categories.

mcq.questionText: A traveller who is stranded and runs out of money far from home may receive Zakah as which category?

options.text: Fi Sabilillah (in the cause of Allah)

mcq.explanation: Ibn as-Sabil is the stranded traveller who lacks means to continue or return, and is entitled to Zakah.

mcq.questionText: Zakat al-Fitr is paid in connection with which event?

options.text: The end of the month of Ramadan
The start of a new business

mcq.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is given at the end of Ramadan, before the Eid al-Fitr prayer.

mcq.questionText: On whom is Zakat al-Fitr obligatory?

options.text: Only on those who own gold and silver
On every Muslim who has food in excess of their needs, including for dependants
Only on those who completed all the fasts

mcq.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is due on every Muslim who has surplus food, paid on behalf of themselves and their dependants, young and old.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following types of wealth is commonly subject to Zakah?

options.text: A person's family house used for living
Gold and silver held above the nisab
A car used only for personal transport

mcq.explanation: Gold and silver above the nisab are subject to Zakah, while personal items of basic need are generally exempt.

mcq.questionText: What is one important social benefit of Zakah in the community?

options.text: It increases the wealth gap between rich and poor
It reduces poverty and helps the needy
It is only for the benefit of the giver
It replaces the need for daily prayer

mcq.explanation: Zakah redistributes wealth, reduces poverty, and strengthens bonds of care between members of society.

mcq.questionText: Zakah on most farm produce and livestock and savings is generally calculated:

options.text: Once a person reaches nisab and the required period is met

mcq.explanation: Zakah becomes due once wealth reaches the nisab and the conditions, such as the lunar year for savings, are met.

mcq.questionText: Which statement about the people who collect and administer Zakah is correct?

options.text: They are forbidden from receiving any Zakah
They may be paid from Zakah as one of the eight categories (Al-Amilin)
They can only be paid from Sadaqah

mcq.explanation: Al-Amilin, the workers appointed to collect and distribute Zakah, are themselves one of the eight eligible categories.

fib.questionText: Zakah is the _____ pillar of Islam.
fib.explanation: Zakah comes after the Shahadah and Salah as the third pillar.

fib.questionText: The minimum amount of wealth on which Zakah becomes due is called _____.
fib.explanation: Nisab is the threshold of wealth above which Zakah is obligatory.

fib.questionText: Unlike Zakah, which is obligatory, _____ is a voluntary act of charity.
fib.explanation: Sadaqah can be given freely at any time, while Zakah is compulsory.

fib.questionText: The Qur'an names _____ categories of people who may receive Zakah.
fib.explanation: There are eight eligible categories of Zakah recipients.

fib.questionText: The charity paid at the end of Ramadan before the Eid prayer is called Zakat al-_____.
fib.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is given before the Eid al-Fitr prayer to purify the fasting person.

fib.questionText: The poor and the needy are referred to in Arabic as Al-Fuqara and Al-_____.
fib.explanation: Al-Fuqara (the poor) and Al-Masakin (the needy) are two of the eight categories.

fib.questionText: The completion of one full lunar year on wealth before paying Zakah is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Hawl is the passing of one lunar year, a condition for Zakah on savings and similar wealth.

fib.questionText: A person burdened with lawful debts they cannot repay is called Al-_____ and may receive Zakah.
fib.explanation: Al-Gharimun are those in debt, one of the eight eligible categories.

fib.questionText: Because it purifies wealth and the soul, the word Zakah literally means purification and _____.
fib.explanation: Zakah means both purification and increase or growth.

fib.questionText: A stranded traveller who needs help to continue his journey is called Ibn as-_____.
fib.explanation: Ibn as-Sabil, the wayfarer, is one of the eight categories of Zakah recipients.

tf.questionText: Zakah is a voluntary act of charity that a Muslim may give whenever they wish.
tf.explanation: Zakah is obligatory with fixed conditions; voluntary giving is called Sadaqah.

tf.questionText: A Muslim must own wealth equal to or above the nisab before Zakah becomes due.
tf.explanation: Reaching the nisab is a condition for Zakah to be obligatory.

tf.questionText: The Qur'an mentions ten categories of people who may receive Zakah.
tf.explanation: The Qur'an mentions eight categories, not ten.

tf.questionText: Zakat al-Fitr is paid at the end of the month of Ramadan.
tf.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is given before the Eid al-Fitr prayer at the close of Ramadan.

tf.questionText: The poor and the needy are among the eight categories entitled to receive Zakah.
tf.explanation: Al-Fuqara and Al-Masakin are two of the eight eligible categories.

tf.questionText: Gold and silver held above the nisab are subject to Zakah.
tf.explanation: Gold and silver above the nisab are among the types of wealth on which Zakah is due.

tf.questionText: Zakah may be paid to a wealthy person simply because they are a friend or relative.
tf.explanation: Zakah must go to the eight eligible categories, not to the wealthy outside those categories.

tf.questionText: One spiritual benefit of Zakah is that it purifies the heart from greed and selfishness.
tf.explanation: Zakah cleanses the soul of stinginess and increases gratitude and generosity.

tf.questionText: Zakah on savings is generally due only after the wealth has been held for one full lunar year.
tf.explanation: The passing of one lunar year (hawl) is a condition for Zakah on savings and similar wealth.

tf.questionText: Sadaqah can only be given in the form of money.
tf.explanation: Sadaqah can take many forms, including a kind word, a smile, or helping others, not only money.

summary.correctAnswer: Purification and growth of wealth and the soul.
summary.explanation: Zakah cleanses wealth and the heart and brings increase and blessing.

summary.correctAnswer: It is the third pillar of Islam.
summary.explanation: Zakah follows the Shahadah and Salah among the five pillars.

summary.correctAnswer: Zakah is obligatory; Sadaqah is voluntary.
summary.explanation: Zakah has fixed conditions and amounts, while Sadaqah is given freely.

summary.correctAnswer: A Muslim who owns wealth above the nisab for a lunar year.
summary.explanation: Faith, ownership of nisab, and possession for one year make Zakah obligatory.

summary.correctAnswer: The minimum amount of wealth on which Zakah is due.
summary.explanation: Wealth below the nisab is not liable for Zakah.

summary.correctAnswer: Eight categories named in the Qur'an.
summary.explanation: These include the poor, the needy, the collectors, and others.

summary.correctAnswer: Charity given at the end of Ramadan before the Eid prayer.
summary.explanation: It purifies the fasting person and provides food for the needy on Eid.

summary.questionText: Types of wealth subject to Zakah
summary.correctAnswer: Gold, silver, savings, trade goods, livestock, and farm produce.
summary.explanation: Zakah applies to growing or stored wealth above the nisab.

summary.correctAnswer: It purifies the heart from greed and increases blessings.
summary.explanation: Giving Zakah cleanses the soul and strengthens faith and gratitude.

summary.correctAnswer: It reduces poverty and unites rich and poor.
summary.explanation: Zakah redistributes wealth and builds compassion in the community.

hoq.questionText: A Muslim trader owns goods and savings well above the nisab but has held them for only six months. Based on the conditions of Zakah, what is the correct ruling for now?

options.text: Zakah is due immediately because the nisab is reached
Zakah is not yet due because one full lunar year has not passed
Zakah is never due on trade goods
Zakah is due only after ten years

hoq.explanation: For savings and trade goods both the nisab and the passing of one lunar year (hawl) are required, so Zakah is not yet due.

hoq.questionText: Why does Islam appoint Al-Amilin (the workers of Zakah) as one of the eight categories who may be paid from Zakah?

options.text: Because collecting and distributing Zakah is real work that deserves payment from it
Because they are relatives of the rich

hoq.explanation: Administering Zakah is a genuine service, so the collectors may be compensated from the Zakah funds even if they are not poor.

hoq.questionText: Two acts of giving are described: one is a fixed yearly duty taken from qualifying wealth, the other is an extra gift given out of kindness at any time. Which terms correctly match them?

options.text: The first is Sadaqah; the second is Zakah
The first is Zakah; the second is Sadaqah

hoq.explanation: The fixed obligatory duty on qualifying wealth is Zakah, while the voluntary kindness given freely is Sadaqah.
